newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - high-grades flat, zeros strong.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - high-grades flat, zeros strong.

text.p: U.S. investment grade bond spreads were unchanged in a quiet session on Tuesday as fresh supply ther held to a trickle, dealers said.
High-yield issuance, meanwhile, resembled that of two weeks ago with deals reportedly well-oversubscribed and trading higher when freed.

Of particular note, Telesystems International Wireless Inc was one of the first successful zero coupon issue to sell in recent months, dealers said. The success may spur more zeros to market, some traders opined, such as the just-announced $300 million issue from Intermedia Communications.

Telesystems' 10-year deal, which was said to have garnered more than $1.0 billion in orders, traded up about two points when dealers lifted syndicate restrictions, traders said. The notes were seen trading in a 54-1/4 bid, 54-3/4 offer market compared with the issued level of 52.595.
"In terms of (small) allocations and in terms of the way it's trading it doesn't surprise me that the deal got so many orders," said one fund manager in New York.
Buysiders said the success of the Telesystems deal was partly attributed to its restructuring with a higher yield to maturity in lieu of the inclusion of a small amount of equity.
The deal, priced with a yield to maturity of 13-1/4 percent, was brought via Goldman, Sachs & Co.

Elsewhere, PTC International Finance's $200 million 10-year senior subordinated discount notes, priced at 59.241 for a yield to maturity of 10.75 percent, traded as high as 62-1/8 before settling back to 61-1/2 bid near the close.
PTC is a Dutch finance company and unit of Poland cellular phone provider Polska Telefonia Cyfrowa. The debt is guaranteed by the latter.
The PTC deal was managed through a Salomon Brothers and Citicorp Securities syndicate.
Despite the success of Tuesday's issues, at least one buysider said not to look for an influx of the structure.

"Issuance of zeros has been running very heavy so I don't think you'll see an increase," one manager said. "If we even keep up the same pace I'll be surprised -- the market has shown a little discipline with Chase Telecom -- but there has been a lot because you have to include the prefundeds."
He added that he will hold extra cash in the portfolio when buying zero coupon bonds.
Other junk bond secondary prices regained footing after a bout of weaker bids on Monday, traders said.
Turning to the high-grade arena, traders reported a lessening of selling pressure in 10-year maturities but spreads remained unchanged on a broad basis as activity was mostly limited to new issues.
Some traders were surprised at the resilience of the corporate bond market given the amount of issuance and historical tightness of spreads.

"There's not as much spread movement as you might think because guys have made money, spreads have tightened and you've seen some paper come out," one trader said, adding that all "fairly" priced new issues have traded well.
Topping new issues, Boston University tapped into demand for century bonds with a 7-5/8 percent issue priced to yield 95 basis points over the Treasury curve via Lehman Brothers.
Also, Coastal Corp unit Colorado Interstate Gas issued $100 million 6.85 percent Baa2/BBB rated 40-year put 10-year debt at par to yield 43 basis points over the curve via Chase Securities.

In the Treasury market, prices ended moderately higher following a stronger-than-expected read of consumer confidence and a successful auction of $15.5 billion. The benchmark 30-year bond was up 5/32 to yield 6.69 percent and the 10-year T-note closed 3/32 higher to yield 6.41 percent.
